title: Onramp Approval State Machine — PRD (WIP)
content:
Context:
This doc proposes a compact state-machine approach for customer VPC onramp approvals and the accompanying audit-log model. Aim is to replace ad-hoc approval flows with a deterministic, machine-verifiable lifecycle that can be sampled for forensic queries and compactly exported to customer SIEMs.

Summary (one-liner):
Introduce an approvals state machine (request -> triage -> signed-assertion -> apply -> reconciled/rolled-back) with immutable audit events, cryptographic receipts for delegated decisions, and a telemetry surface for SLA/latency sampling.

Goals:
- Deterministic approval transitions with minimal manual gating points.
- Compact audit record per change (<= 4KB compressed) that captures evidence pointers and operator assertions.
- Clear operator UX for canary vs full apply, with replayable checkpoints.
- Exportable proofs for customer-managed networking (VPC handoffs) and legal/compliance needs.

Non-goals:
- This does not design the entire attestation schema for on-prem air-gapped installs (follow-up doc).
- Not handling full SIEM ingestion pipelines — we provide export hooks and canonical compact JSON lines.

Proposed state machine (textual):
- NEW_REQUEST: created by customer or automation. payload includes change blob ref, initiator id, requested window.
- PENDING_TRIAGE: assigned to an operator or auto-triage rule. may have parallel checks (ip-allowlist, route-validation).
- AWAITING_APPROVAL: human approval required (multisig optional) or delegated auto-approve.
- APPROVED_SIGNATURE: approval recorded as a signed assertion (operator id + key id + signature).
- APPLYING: orchestration in progress (idempotent apply operations, with stepwise checkpoints).
- APPLIED: target state observed by reconciliation. emits reconciliation evidence.
- ROLLBACK_REQUESTED: triggered by failed checks or operator cancel.
- ROLLED_BACK / RESOLVED: final states.
- EXPIRED: request timed out; cleanup/archival emitted.

Transition rules (notes):
- Every transition emits an audit event (see audit schema below).
- Signed transitions (APPROVED_SIGNATURE) must include operator KMS key id or HSM reference and a compact proof-of-origin (hash chain element).
- All APPLYING steps must be idempotent and reference a change-token so retries are safe.
- Triage can attach automatic sampling decisions (sample=high/low) which control retention and debug snapshot behavior.

Audit event model (compact fields):
- event_id: uuid
- request_id: uuid
- timestamp_iso: rfc3339
- actor: user/service principal
- action: transition name
- evidence_refs: list of short refs (s3://, gs://, or internal blob id)
- signature_meta: (optional) key_ref | sig_alg | sig_value_short (base64-compact)
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- sample_bucket: none | low | high
- trace_id: correlates to orchestration pipeline
Notes: keep evidence_refs short pointers; actual artifact lives in long-term storage or customer-accessible bucket.

Operator UX sketch (painpoints / proposed fixes):
- Operators need a single pane showing pending approvals, risk score, and quick evidence links. include one-click roll-forward and one-click safe-rollback.
- Approve flow should include pre-baked checklist from triage step and an optional free-text justification that becomes part of the signed assertion.
- If auto-approve is used, generate a synthetic signed assertion with automation identity and attach policy id.

Telemetry & sampling plan:
- Metrics to emit: time_in_state (per-state p50/p95/p99), approval_latency, apply_success_rate, rollback_rate, evidence_fetch_latency.
- Sampling tiers: low (retain audit headers only for 30d), high (retain full evidence bundle for 180d).
- Route error traces to console with a single sample of full evidence per incident by default.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Signed assertions must not embed PII; free-text justification should be redaction-aware.
- Evidence storage must support customer-managed keys when requested (KMS integration).
- Signatures: prefer asymmetric keys (RSA/ECDSA) stored in customer or Redwood HSM depending on deployment tier.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experimental): implement state machine in a sandbox control plane for Beta partners, no legal binding receipts. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1 (pilot): add signed assertions + export hook to customer S3; trial with 3 customers. (4–6 sprints)
- Phase 2 (GA): retention controls, SLA targets, integrations with SIEM and KMS/HSM. (quarterly milestone)

Open questions / risks:
- How to balance compact audit size vs usefulness for forensic: what evidence types are mandatory vs optional?
- Delegated approvals economics: who pays for long-term evidence retention?
- Replay fidelity for on-prem: can we assume network state snapshots are available to produce reconciled evidence?

Next steps / action items:
- Aisha: prototype minimal event envelope and sample signed assertion (JIRA: JIRA-PD-789). due 2025-04-01.
- Marcus: mockup operator console approvals list, include rollback UX. due 2025-04-08.
- Carlos & Evelyn: map current triage checks to auto-triage rules and sampling buckets. due 2025-04-15.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; I expect follow-ups for: schema evolution rules, legal wording for signed receipts, and on-prem evidence routing.
- Feedback: add comments inline or drop directly into the linked Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-1234) — prefer technical notes on the event envelope and signature format.

Rough appendix (example audit event line):
{event_id: "evt-1a2b3c", request_id: "req-9f8e", timestamp_iso: "2025-03-14T16:22:01Z", actor: "operator:marcus", action: "APPROVED_SIGNATURE", evidence_refs: ["bkt://evidence/req-9f8e/checksum:sha256-..."], signature_meta: "kref=projects/p-kms/key/42;alg=ECDSA_P256;sig=b64:...", outcome: "success", sample_bucket: "high", trace_id: "trace-3344"}

(end of draft)
